scope: Read-only code review of the frozen v4 files listed in input_manifest.json. I ran nothing, edited nothing and hashed nothing. Every hash below is copied from the manifest or test.log. Source, recipe and export approvals are separate and are not given here.

binding.before_after_test_run: The before/after hashes are in test.log:1 and test.log:99, not in the manifest. Both hashes are the same before and after the run and match the manifest. Only pesuqei.py and the test file were hashed. authoring.py, morning_shared.py and morning_witnesses.py have manifest hashes but no before/after hashes. The run used the ~/.codex worktree, and nothing in the log ties that worktree's HEAD to the base commit.
binding.results: 75 passed, 29 subtests passed (test.log:98). There are 19 pesuqei node IDs (test.log:69-92), matching the frozen test file.

evidence: Existing-file gate (pesuqei.py:259-270): it scans every element through root.iter(), including the root, for @corresp in the target set. The set holds the repeat targets plus any range targets that have no 'en' witness. Regenerated paths are skipped. It runs before verify_existing_outputs and before writing (main:315).

In-batch gate (pesuqei.py:205-209): it counts every English-project element whose @corresp equals the target, from any element type. It requires exactly 1 match, and that match must be a tei:milestone. So an in-batch div/@corresp provider fails closed.

Regression (test:417-419): an older English file whose root div has corresp=IDENTITY is rejected with 'bypass the repeat guard'. The milestone case and the regenerated-path exemption are also covered (test:413-416).
residual_low: There is no synthetic test showing an in-batch non-milestone provider being rejected. The code fails closed, but nothing exercises that path.

Both gates match the target only exactly. An older English provider that maps a containing unit (for example the chapter URN) or a range is not caught. Whether refdb resolves a verse through such a provider is still unverified, as in v3 risk #2.

verified: item.ranges produces one canonical call per span. In expanded mode every span is called, unqualified (pesuqei.py:167-169). In documentary mode a language is called only if it is in span.witnesses, so a language that lacks the span is skipped (105-108).

build_documents rejects repeat combined with ranges (184-185). It rejects empty witnesses or witnesses outside the unit's languages (186-188). It sends each span target through call() so qualified or non-text URNs are rejected before anything is built (189).
Range targets with no 'en' witness are added to the existing-provider gate (262-263).

The generated E2E test (test:342-399) puts psalms/8/2 (Hebrew only) between bilingual verses 1 and 3. For both the expanded spine and the documentary Hebrew service it asserts: PARTn-he appears once each; PART2-en is absent while 1 and 3 are present; the v2 transclusion is a single call with an empty parallel counterpart; and English page changes are n7, n8, n9, checked alongside the repeat assertions (HE×2, EN×1).

findings.title: Range witnesses are not checked against the generated witness documents
findings.detail: span.witnesses is only checked to be a subset of the unit's language keys (pesuqei.py:187). Nothing checks that the English witness document built for the unit actually lacks an element with @corresp equal to a span target marked Hebrew only. witness_document emits whatever corresp the approved readings carry (morning_witnesses.py:108-118). The existing-provider gate skips regenerated files (pesuqei.py:264-267). So if the recipe marks v2 as ['he'] but the English readings contain v2, an unguarded English v2 provider is written in this batch. The documentary-parallel and expanded output would then show English for a verse declared Hebrew only, and no gate fires. This is the range version of the in-batch repeat binding at 205-209. The opposite mismatch (a span lists 'en' but has no English provider) emits an English service call that won't resolve, so any failure there would only come at compile time.
findings.required_change: In build_documents, after corrections and before guards, check every span. The set of languages whose generated document for the unit has any element with @corresp == span.target must equal set(span.witnesses). For targets without an 'en' witness, also require zero English-project in-batch matches across all documents. Add synthetic regressions for both mismatch directions.

findings.detail: There are no tests for the repeat+range rejection (184-185), the witness-subset or empty-witness rejection (186-188), or a qualified range target. Span targets are not checked to fall inside the unit, to be in order, to be free of overlap, or to be unique across the order. In expanded mode expanded_target is silently ignored when ranges are present. These depend on recipe review.

prior_findings: N1, N3-N7 and F1-F14 are unchanged from the v3 review; their residuals carry over (registry acceptance of the new feature and j:conditional placement not read; day-one Hebrew transclusion fallback; baseline_commit only checked as 40 hex characters).
remaining_material: After writing and refreshing refdb, confirm exactly one English provider per repeat target and none for any Hebrew-only range target, including any provider reached through a containing unit.
separate_approvals_not_given: Recipe: order, which item is hebrew_only_repeat, range witness lists, templates byte-identical to the frozen spines with verified baseline commits

Export: books --check on both profiles, plus documentary Hebrew, documentary parallel and expanded PDF/HTML checks (English only at the first occurrence, no other translator, backlinks, notes, bookmark, parallel mode without the fallback warning, and the Hebrew-only v2 with no English counterpart or page)

model_effort.actual_exposed: Model Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5). The runtime showed reasoning effort 10 (low), not medium. No other effort setting was exposed.
